preconditions: Loader session, idempotency and TTL state is held in one fake module-data store.
Every read compares the stored request fingerprint with the current input.
scenarios.input: Begin an upload, retry the same key, reuse the key for another destination, change the input fingerprint and advance time across the session/idempotency TTL.
scenarios.action: Call BeginUpload, ValidUpload and TTL-dependent reads through the Loader application service.
scenarios.expected_result: Idempotency is principal and key scoped; distinct keys never collapse; a changed fingerprint is rejected; session and idempotency records remain aligned across commit and result retention.
scenarios.expected_state: Only the original upload session is replayed for its key, and expired sessions are not returned by the user-facing API.

preconditions: Parts are recorded with stable keys, exact staging references, size and SHA-256.
A Core final-file request can be pending, ready, failed or not found after an ambiguous response.
scenarios.input: Write all parts, commit, retry the commit, hold a session with a pending Core request, then recover pending, ready and failed Core commit states.
scenarios.action: Call part-write/commit/recovery operations on the Loader application service with a fake Core file API.
scenarios.expected_result: A successful commit is idempotent; pending preserves session and parts; ready records the returned file ID; failed/not found aborts; gaps, duplicates and checksum mismatches never publish a file.
scenarios.expected_state: No partially visible Core file is created; recovered sessions end in committed or aborted state with matching durable records.

preconditions: Cleanup jobs are durable and have no TTL; staging bytes and part records are removed only after a terminal Core state.
Cleanup identity and session/job state compatibility are verified before deletion.
scenarios.input: Abort a session, try to extend an expired session with a part write, rotate cleanup past a pending Core commit and present mismatched or already-removed cleanup jobs.
scenarios.action: Call cleanup and expired-upload operations with fake Core state and bounded cursors.
scenarios.expected_result: Abort schedules durable cleanup, expired uploads reject part writes, pending jobs do not block later jobs, identity mismatches stop cleanup and a job removed by another replica is an idempotent success.
scenarios.expected_state: Only exact staging references and part records for resolved uploads are deleted; no ambiguous Core request is cleaned prematurely.

preconditions: loader.max_concurrent_commits bounds commit slots and commit_timeout bounds slot waiting.
Core session authentication and current group rights are checked again before commit; the local session cache is bounded by entries, bytes, TTL and revision.
scenarios.input: Exceed commit concurrency, observe admission metrics, revoke group access before commit, authenticate an inactive principal and evict a cache entry by count, bytes, TTL and revision.
scenarios.action: Call commit, admission, authentication and session-cache operations through the Loader application service.
scenarios.expected_result: Excess commits fail closed without session mutation, revoked rights block publication, inactive principals are rejected and stale/oversized cache entries are never reused.
scenarios.expected_state: Every admission and authorization decision is fail-closed and the cache remains a bounded hint validated against Core revision.

preconditions: A disposable PostgreSQL/S3 stack and a live Router/Core API built from this checkout are available.
The upload route is Loader-backed with server-owned destination, MIME allowlist, byte limits, staging path and idempotency key.
scenarios.input: Upload a multipart file through the exact public route, kill and restart the Loader, resume commit, verify checksum and group access and request the registered exact file GET.
scenarios.action: Run the tagged HTTP e2e flow with LOADER_TEST_DISPOSABLE=1 and the declared Core/uploader base URLs.
scenarios.expected_result: Bytes become visible only after verified Core finalization, restart/resume is safe, revoked access prevents file creation and FileSet membership never grants byte access.
scenarios.expected_state: Without the isolated disposable Core/PostgreSQL/S3 stack the scenario is not executed and is never reported as pass.
scenarios.blocker: Disposable Loader/Core environment not provided: require LOADER_TEST_DISPOSABLE=1, LOADER_TEST_CORE_BASE_URL, LOADER_TEST_UPLOADER_BASE_URL and LOADER_TEST_TIMEOUT. No live working API is used.
